setup.heading: Turn on two-step verification
setup.forcedIntro: As an administrator you must turn on two-step verification first: after the password, logging in will also ask for a code from an authenticator app on your phone.
setup.scan: Scan the code with an authenticator app (for example Aegis, Google Authenticator or 2FAS).
setup.qr: QR code for the authenticator app
setup.manual: Can't scan it? Enter the key by hand:
setup.clock: The server's clock and this device's differ by {{count}} seconds: if the code is refused, check the time on the server and on your phone.

codes.heading: Recovery codes
codes.intro: If you lose the app you can log in with one of these codes. Each works once, and they will not be shown again.
codes.keep: Save them in a safe place (for example a password manager).

settings.off: Not active. Recommended if the app can be reached from the Internet.
settings.onNotice: Two-step verification is on. Your other sessions were logged out.
settings.offText: You will log in with the password alone. Your other sessions are logged out.
settings.codesText: Ten new codes replace the old ones, which stop working. Your other sessions are logged out.
settings.codeHint: The 6 digits of your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.

notice.text: Your two-step verification was turned off on {{date}}. You can turn it on again in Settings.

admin.heading: Turn off the 2FA of {{name}}?
admin.text: {{name}} will log in with the password alone, is logged out on every device and will see a notice with the date. Do it only if {{name}} lost the phone and the recovery codes.
